claims.text: As-cast or conventionally processed HfZrTi HEA has relatively coarse grains.
As-cast or conventionally processed HfZrTi HEA has a less optimized dislocation structure.
Multi-stage forging or rolling above the recrystallization temperature can improve the HfZrTi HEA.
A progressive deformation reduction of 50–80% is an appropriate processing range for the proposed treatment.
A controlled annealing step at approximately 700–800 K is appropriate after deformation.
Processing in an inert or reducing atmosphere will avoid oxidation during treatment.
The proposed thermomechanical treatment will refine the grain and subgrain structures of HfZrTi.
The proposed treatment will produce a more uniform dislocation distribution.
Deformation under the proposed conditions will promote dynamic recovery or dynamic recrystallization.
The subsequent annealing step will further refine the HfZrTi microstructure.
The refined microstructure will improve the alloy's ability to deform plastically.
The refined microstructure will improve the alloy's ability to arrest crack propagation.
The treated HfZrTi HEA will exhibit greater percentage elongation than the untreated alloy.
The treated HfZrTi HEA will exhibit higher fracture toughness than the untreated alloy.
The treated HfZrTi HEA will retain yield strength comparable to that of the untreated alloy.
The magnitude of improvement depends sensitively on deformation reduction ratio and annealing temperature and time.
Excessive processing may cause undesirable grain coarsening.
Processing-induced texture effects may negate the proposed ductility and toughness benefits.
